FINDING_ID: RA_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.assign()` and `reassign()` implicitly assume `model_id` is unique, but neither method validates it. If two `ModelSpec` entries share the same `model_id`, `scores[m.model_id] = ...`, `role_map[...] = ...`, and `_failure_history={m.model_id: [] ...}` will silently overwrite earlier entries. This can collapse multiple physical models into one logical slot, produce fewer assigned roles than input models, and corrupt failure-history attribution. Because the rest of the system keys all downstream state by `model_id`, this is a hard correctness issue in the Role Assignment area.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate uniqueness of `model_id` at `assign()` entry, e.g. compare `len({m.model_id for m in models})` to `len(models)` and raise `ValueError` on duplicates. Ideally also enforce non-empty IDs.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: RA_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` accepts any `active_models: Set[str]` and does not validate that `self.pm_model_id` is a member. It always forces `new_map = {self.pm_model_id: Role.PM}` even when the PM is absent from the active set. This creates an inconsistent role map mixing inactive and active models: `remaining_ids` is derived from `active_models`, but the returned mapping always contains the locked PM regardless of liveness. In a failure scenario where the PM has been removed from active execution, Role Assignment will still claim it is assigned, which can mislead Area 2/3 consumers that interpret `role_map` as the active role partition. Prior findings covered stale model lists generally, but this specific invariant break inside `reassign()` appears unreported.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce one of two explicit policies:  
1. HARD invariant: require `pm_model_id in active_models` and raise if violated; or  
2. Separate active-role mapping from global locked-role mapping, so `reassign()` returns only active assignments and PM lock is stored separately.  
Document the invariant and assert it.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: RA_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` bases the COL/no-COL decision on `len(self._models) >= 3` instead of the number of active models. This is related to prior finding CC2_F029, but there is a second distinct consequence: when total configured models are at least 3 but active non-PM models collapse to 1, `best_col_id` is still promoted to `COL`, yielding a role map with `PM` + `COL` and zero `PAR`, even though there is no remaining participant population to collate over. The initial `assign()` semantics use pool cardinality to decide whether a COL role exists; `reassign()` instead uses original configured cardinality, so role meaning drifts as the active pool shrinks.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base COL existence on active cardinality, preferably `if len(active_models) >= 3:` (or equivalent explicit policy if PM excluded from the count). Keep the criterion identical between `assign()` and `reassign()`.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: RA_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: `get_ordering()` returns rankings from `self.capability_scores`, but `capability_scores` is computed only once in `assign()` and is never refreshed in `reassign()`. Since `reassign()` recomputes COL scores using a different `pool_max` restricted to active models plus a failure-history penalty, the stored ordering can diverge from the actual role-selection logic after the first round. Any consumer using `get_ordering(Role.COL)` as an explanation, audit record, or validation of current assignments will receive stale and materially false rankings. This is a local Role Assignment state-consistency bug, distinct from broader live-fingerprint issues already reported elsewhere.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either recompute and persist current round scores during `reassign()` (including whether penalties are applied), or rename `capability_scores`/`get_ordering()` to make clear they are initial-assignment-only. Best fix is to track both static base scores and current effective scores separately.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: RA_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: `record_failure()` appends an entry whenever called, but there is no round index, deduplication, or cardinality control. `reassign()` interprets `_failure_history[mid]` as a per-round sequence and computes `phi_hist = mean(failures)`. If a caller records multiple failures for the same model in one round, or omits a call in another round, the penalty ceases to represent “mean failure rate across rounds” and instead becomes “mean over arbitrary event count.” This biases role reassignment unpredictably and can permanently over-penalize models after retry-heavy rounds.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Store failure history keyed by round index (`Dict[str, Dict[int, bool]]`) or provide `record_failure(model_id, round_idx, failed)` with overwrite semantics per round. Then compute the mean over rounds, not event appends.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: RA_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.47  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_homogeneous()` does not actually validate the documented tie-breaking behavior. The docstring says “tie-breaking assigns PM,” but the check only asserts exactly one PM exists and all PM scores are equal. A broken implementation that chooses an arbitrary or unstable PM across runs would still pass. This weak validator can mask regressions in one of the core Role Assignment invariants: deterministic tie resolution.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Strengthen the validator to assert the selected PM matches the lexicographic tie-break rule for identical-score models, or at minimum verify deterministic selection based on model order/defined comparator across repeated runs.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: RA_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.44  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48  
DESCRIPTION: `round_idx` is accepted by `reassign()` but never used. The method docstring says the argument is “for failure history,” implying round-aware behavior, but actual penalty computation uses the entire append-only `_failure_history` list with no round filtering. This is an API/implementation mismatch that invites incorrect caller assumptions and obscures the fact that the penalty is lifetime-average rather than round-indexed.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `round_idx` from the signature and docs, or use it to compute a bounded/windowed/history-to-date penalty with explicit semantics.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: RA_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.39  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46  
DESCRIPTION: `remaining_ids = [mid for mid in active_models if mid != self.pm_model_id]` iterates a `set`, so order is nondeterministic. While `best_col_id` is chosen by `max(col_scores, ...)`, ties in `col_scores` are resolved by insertion order of the dict, which here depends on set iteration order rather than the documented deterministic tie-break rule. That means `reassign()` can select different COL models across processes or hash seeds when adjusted scores are exactly equal. `assign()` explicitly implements deterministic tie-breaking; `reassign()` does not.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Sort `remaining_ids` deterministically and apply the same `_tie_break_key()` used in `assign()`, e.g. choose `max(candidates, key=lambda m: (col_scores[mid], self._tie_break_key(model)))`.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: RA_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.33  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.40  
DESCRIPTION: [SPECULATIVE] Cross-component risk from this area: `reassign()` mutates `self.role_map` in place and returns the same conceptual structure without any snapshot/versioning. If Area 2/3 retains references or derives allocations concurrently/asynchronously from `role_map`, callers may observe partially updated role state across rounds. The provided artifact does not show concurrent use, so this remains unverified from scope, but the in-place mutable shared state is a plausible integration hazard.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Return an immutable snapshot (or copy-on-write dict) and treat role assignments as round-versioned state. Update shared manager state only at round boundaries.  
VERIFIED: FALSE
